thread.title: Chegg May Be Overvalued... So What? - Chegg, Inc. (NYSE:CHGG)

author: Nimish Garg
title: Chegg May Be Overvalued... So What? - Chegg, Inc. (NYSE:CHGG)
text:
I'd like to argue that Chegg (NYSE: CHGG ) is a high-growth, high-risk stock whose qualitative upsides outweigh its quantitative downsides. Chegg is a company that I and tens of millions of college students ( 40 million , to be precise) hold very dearly to our hearts. Not only does it grant solutions to tens of millions of textbooks, but after acquisition of companies such as CourseRank, Notehall, Zinch, and most recently Imagine Easy Solutions, which respectively provide a course rating system, access to class notes, a service that matches students to recruiters, and tutoring services, Chegg is devouring the college student niche. Investors have already begun to realize this, leading its share price to increment by 116% over this past year. In this article, I'll provide a breakdown of this up-and-comer, namely, its audience/industry, fundamentals, and competitive advantage.
Audience/Industry Chegg targets college students, and its consumer base is only set to grow. Currently, 20.67 million students are enrolled in public and private colleges in the U.S, and this number is estimated to reach 22.63 million - an 8.66% increase. Moreover, so far Chegg has mainly marketed itself to U.S. students; however, over 207 million students are enrolled in higher education worldwide, a number that has doubled since 2000. After all, the unemployment rate for college grads is 2.5%, as opposed to a 7.4% rate for high school dropouts. These statistics serve to show that Chegg has ample room to grow.
Chegg is a service that is no longer a luxury, but rather a necessity for college students. With the average college student being severely overworked, and with 9.5% feeling depressed (as opposed to 6.1% five years ago), students have turned to services such as Chegg to seek help from tutors, read clear explanations of problems, and recently, copy Chegg answers for problem sets - a significant component of their grade - as the pressure from parents, professors, and recruiters for good grades has swelled .
Furthermore, Chegg is part of an industry that is relatively secure from fluctuations in the economy. If the economy is doing well, people will continue to educate themselves in pursuit of a higher-paid job. If the economy is doing badly, people whose skills are no longer critical and are unemployed will take the opportunity to re-train themselves using services such as Chegg. In this way, Chegg is a good hedge.
Fundamentals Chegg's fundamentals are mixed. It is still unprofitable, but the company is cutting its losses each year. Chegg has struggled to make a profit on its investments in the past, yielding an EPS of -$0.04 during the quarter ending in June 2017 and -$0.08 during the quarter ending in September 2017.
Still, it's been doing better recently, with the $0.06 EPS in December 2017 and $0.01 EPS in March 2018, likely attributed to its lessening operating costs (as the authors to the solutions to most textbooks have mostly been paid). In all these cases, however, the company has beaten market expectations.
In terms of valuation, Chegg still isn't profitable with a negative net income and weaker than competitors, with the stock at 54.31x cash flow and 10.89x sales, as compared to its competitors' average 21.63x cash flow and 5.48x sales.
In terms of its bottom line, though, the company is strengthening because of the digital transition . Chegg has sold $171,268,000 worth of stock over the year. The adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization was $46.4 million in 2017, as opposed to $21 million in 2016. Its services revenues grew by 44% to $185.7 million. Overall revenue increased by 16.6%, outpacing the revenue growth of its competitors.
Most notably, its net income increased from -$42,245,000 to -$20,283,000. Although the net income is still negative, the total amount of cash flow from operating activities has doubled, while capital expenditures barely changed. 80% of cash flow being used is for highly promising investments such as tutors or acquisitions, whose benefits are discussed in the section below. This correlates with Chegg's income statement.
Although its gross profit is abnormally high (with total revenue being 3x its cost of revenue) as compared to a company like Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ), whose total revenue is 1.5x its cost of revenue, Chegg is investing so much into R&D (0.33x its total revenue). Moreover, the company is really trying to get its name out there, as its Selling General and Administrative costs are 0.5x the total revenue, which is vital, as there is a large, untapped consumer base discussed in the first section, coupled with an aggressive management. These numbers are much larger than those of name brands like Apple, but it's to be expected for an ambitious company.
In this way, because capital expenditures and cost of revenue are so low, we see that Chegg is becoming a more efficient company, as its ROE greatly increased from the past year (though it still trails its competitors).
Moreover, with no debt and a quick ratio of 4.33, Chegg can cover its short-term cash needs. In fact, its assets are 8x its liabilities, as compared to a gold standard like Apple, whose assets are 1.5x its liabilities.
It's safe to say that buying Chegg isn't for the faint of heart, especially when there are so many safer, profitable options out on the market. But with many of its metrics improving by 50% yoy, and the company investing so much into R&D and acquisitions, Chegg is definitely a mover.
Competitive Advantage Chegg is led by a veteran group of executives. Dan Rosensweig, former COO of Yahoo, has assumed the mantle as CEO. Backed with support from a growth management including Mike Osier , a leader at Netflix before its IPO, helping it grow from 100k to 15 million subscribers, Chegg is aggressively swallowing up the student support market. These leaders have recognized the company's susceptible audience, adding more features, reaching more students internationally, and doing everything possible to ensure the best experience for its subscribers.
Moreover, recognizing that universities are beginning to underinvest in office hours for students, its management is focusing on the growth of Chegg tutors - something the company cites to be its biggest growth potential. Here's where its main competitive advantage lies: although the company has multiple competitors in many parts of its core business, such as Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN ) in textbook rentals, tutors.com in tutoring, EasyBib for citations, Glassdoor for internships, etc., Chegg is the integrated solution for a student's four years at college.
The same student who is renting a textbook also is likely aware of Chegg Study to get homework help and view solutions. If these solutions don't make sense, they can receive clarifications through Chegg tutors. Once finished with their problem sets or research papers, they can cite their sources using Chegg's Easy Solutions. And once the time arrives, receive internships on Internships.com, a Chegg service.
No one else has that. No other competitors have the whole package that can sustain a student for four years. And because Chegg is so widespread, the business, as long as its acquisitions are related and serve to augment the students' experience, is easily more profitable than any of its competitors. After all, that’s what you get when your acquisition costs plummet.
I like to call this the Facebook (NASDAQ: FB ) approach . Facebook succeeded and defeated competitors such as Myspace and Zynga because it went above and beyond to fulfill its goal - connecting people. From being launched in a college dorm room, it acquired dozens of businesses, diversified the ways it connected, and made itself the leading social media platform. Chegg is doing the same thing; although its consumer base in only 300 million as opposed to 7 billion (Facebook), that's a sizable amount, and it will be a fruitful endeavor because of the sheer lack of competition.
College students have been growing dependent on Chegg and will use it more as workloads at college increase, similar to how people grew dependent on Facebook to connect with their friends in a variety of manners. Based on my research and my own personal experience, Chegg deeply cares about its students and will give them the resources they need to succeed - and this is its competitive advantage that, in time, will propel Chegg to unimaginable heights.
Disclosure: I/we have no positions in any stocks mentioned, and no plans to initiate any positions within the next 72 hours.
